newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Friday, with no sales expected following this week's heavy volume which cleaned up most showlists, according to feedlot sources.
Prices this week were mostly at $66.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week, supported by a winter storm that produced dangerously cold wind chills.
The storm substantially reduced weight gains, with some feedlots reporting declines of 20 to 25 lbs per head.
Cattle were expected to adjust to the weather, but the first major storm of the season took its toll, they said.
Temperatures were moderating Friday in the Panhandle and Kansas and were expected to continue warming into the mid-50s to lower 60s degrees Fahrenheit this weekend, sources said.

Pen conditions were not expected to deteriorate as temperatures warm, becasue light winds should dry the ground as it thaws. There also was not much moisture associated with this week's storm south of Nebraska, some cattle feeders said.
Showlists next week could be smaller because of heavy sales the past two weeks, sources noted.
